Article Title: NMC orders monthly reporting of student suicides by medical colleges
Article Text:
For each suicide or unnatural death, colleges have to report the student's course/year, date and place of occurrence, police intimation, FIR status, institutional inquiry and corrective measures.

NEW DELHI: The National Medical Commission (NMC) has directed medical colleges to maintain updated records of student suicides and unnatural deaths and submit a certified Action Taken Report (ATR) every month, following Supreme Court directions on student mental health and safety. It has also asked institutions to fill vacant faculty and key administrative posts within four months.The commission has marked the compliance exercise “MOST URGENT” and asked institutions to accord it top priority.The move comes amid a rise in student suicides. An IHBAS presentation by Dr Om Prakash, Professor of Psychiatry and Head, Department of Geriatric Mental Health, citing NCRB data, said 14,488 student deaths by suicide were recorded in 2024, up 4.3% from 13,892 in 2023. The number rose from 8,068 in 2014 to 14,488 in 2024, an increase of around 80% over the decade. More than 1.15 lakh student deaths by suicide were recorded during 2015-24.For each suicide or unnatural death, colleges have to report the student's course/year, date and place of occurrence, police intimation, FIR status, institutional inquiry and corrective measures.The NMC has also sought department-wise details of sanctioned, filled and vacant faculty posts, non-teaching vacancies and key administrative positions, including dean/director, medical superintendent, registrar, wardens and counsellors.Colleges have been given four months to fill vacant faculty and key administrative posts, with special recruitment drives for reserved posts. The compliance format also requires 24x7 access to qualified medical assistance on campus or within 1 km.The IHBAS presentation highlights the role of faculty as “gatekeepers”, who can often notice changes in attendance, academic performance, withdrawal or behaviour. Faculty are advised to recognise warning signs, approach distressed students, ask directly about suicidal thoughts, facilitate referral and follow up, without taking on the role of therapists.It also cautions against attributing suicide to a single trigger such as examination failure, relationship problems or social media. Academic pressure, fear of failure, bullying, ragging or harassment, discrimination, social isolation and financial difficulties are among the factors identified as contributing to vulnerability.The NMC said information submitted by institutions will be consolidated to monitor compliance with the Supreme Court's directions and submitted to the Ministry of Education as required.
Article Summary: The national medical commission has directed medical colleges to maintain updated records of student suicides and unnatural deaths. It has also asked institutions to fill vacant faculty and key administrative posts within four months. The move comes amid a rise in student suicides.

Article Title: ‘They opposed Ambedkar’s Constitution, wanted Manusmriti’: Owaisi targets RSS, BJP
Article Text:
His remarks come amid an intensifying political confrontation between the BJP and Congress over the Manusmriti and its place in India's social and constitutional discourse.

NEW DELHI: AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi has launched a sharp attack on the RSS and BJP over the Manusmriti, questioning their commitment to the Indian Constitution. He accused them of historically favouring the ancient text over the document adopted by the country.Owaisi made the remarks during his address at the Jalsa-e-Rahmatul-lil-Alameen at Darussalam .n Hyderabad on the occasion of the 1501st Eid Milad-un-Nabi. He targeted the RSS over its reported opposition to the Constitution drafted by Dr BR Ambedkar and contrasted the organisation's position with that of Muslim freedom fighters during British rule."I am asking those associated with the RSS about Manusmriti. Is it not true that on November 26, 1949, we adopted the Constitution? Yet, four days later, on November 30, a mouthpiece of the RSS published a complaint against it, stating that it wasn't a constitution at all and that it should have been the Manusmriti. They had issues with the Constitution drafted by Babasaheb Ambedkar," Owaisi said.The AIMIM chief also attacked Hindutva ideologue VD Savarkar, referring to his correspondence with the British during his imprisonment in the Andaman cellular jail."Savarkar was in support of Manusmriti. While he was in Andaman jail, he was writing letters to the British, saying, 'I am with you, please release me.' But what were we doing? Allama Fazl-e-Haq Khairabadi was also in jail; he endured hardships but never wrote a 'love letter' to the British. Instead, he issued a fatwa for Jihad against them. Even today, his grave stands in the Andaman as a testament," he asserted.Owaisi further sought to highlight the role of Muslim figures in India's freedom struggle. He claimed that the first prisoner sent to the Andaman Islands was Maulvi Alauddin, the Imam of Hyderabad's Mecca Masjid."Listen, BJP and RSS people, who was the first prisoner in Andaman? It was not your father, grandfather, or ancestor. It was Hyderabad's Maulvi Alauddin, the Imam of Mecca Masjid. He was the first prisoner," Owaisi told the gathering.His remarks come amid an intensifying political confrontation between the BJP and Congress over the Manusmriti and its place in India's social and constitutional discourse.The BJP has recently targeted Congress leader and Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi over his criticism of the Manusmriti. It accused Rahul of making statements that undermine India's traditions, cultural heritage and democratic institutions. Several BJP leaders, including chief ministers, have alleged that Rahul Gandhi's remarks sought to "belittle" India's civilisational values.At an event titled 'Chhatron ki Goonj' in Pune, Rahul Gandhi criticised a passage attributed to the Manusmriti concerning women's independence."This is a direct quote from the Manusmriti, and these words are a shame, because these words should never ever have been spoken," Gandhi said after quoting the passage: "In childhood, a female belongs to her father. In youth, she belongs to her husband. When her lord is dead, she belongs to her sons. A woman must never be independent."Rahul also called for an end to patriarchal structures, telling female students that the country needs to "smash the prevailing patriarchy" to achieve genuine empowerment for women.The exchange has brought the Manusmriti back into the centre of a wider political debate over constitutional values, social equality and competing interpretations of India's cultural and political history.
Article Summary: Aimim president asaduddin owaisi questions rss' commitment to the indian constitution. He accused them of historically favouring the ancient text over the document adopted by the country. His remarks come amid an intensifying political confrontation between the bjp and congress over the manusmriti.

Article Title: ‘Separatist’ OCI card holder in SC, seeks nod to visit Kashmir
Article Text:
Appearing for Qazi, senior advocate Parag Tripathi told SC that the 82-year-old medical practitioner had visited India in the past.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday sought the Union govt’s response to US-based octogenarian — Khalid Jahangir Qazi — an OCI card holder accused by India of peddling pro-Pakistan propaganda and being sympathetic to Kashmir i separatists, who is seeking permission to visit Kashmir to attend wedding functions in his sister’s family.Appearing for Qazi, whose OCI card cancellation was annulled by a single judge bench of Delhi high court and appeals against which is pending before a division bench, senior advocate Parag Tripathi told a bench led by CJI Surya Kant that the 82-year-old medical practitioner had visited India in the past and given his age and that of his relatives, this may be the last time he would be able to visit Kashmir and be with family members.“He is ready to give an undertaking that during his visit, he would not indulge in any political activity,” Tripathi said. This persuaded the bench to issue notice to the Centre and sought its response by Sep 7, the next date of hearing. The Delhi high court had earlier rejected his plea to visit India.Qazi stands accused of ‘pro-Pakistan propaganda’ by the Indian Consulate in New York. Indian govt had cancelled his OCI card in May 2023 because of activities which are “inimical to sovereignty and security of India”, and blacklisted him under the Foreigners Act. In Nov 2024, a single judge bench of the Delhi HC had quashed the cancellation of his OCI card saying that Qazi was not given a fair hearing prior to the cancellation.
Article Summary: Qazi stands accused of ‘pro-pakistan propaganda’ by the indian consulate in new york. Indian govt had cancelled his oci card in may 2023 because of activities which are ‘inimical to sovereignty and security of india’

Article Title: Congress’s pellet gun fire draws BJP 1984 counter
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Demand from opposition MPs, including Priyanka Gandhi Vadra , that a parliamentary committee take up the issue of use of “excessive” force against protesting students led to a fiery exchange at its meeting on Tuesday as a BJP member brought up the “glorification” of anti-Sikh riots convict Sajjan Kumar to counter the Congress’s move to raise a matter that was not part of the agenda of “crimes against children”.Sources said Congress MP Ajay Maken had written to parliamentary committee on home affairs chairperson and BJP MP Radha Mohan Das Agrawal on Aug 5 saying the discussion should include the allegations against the Delhi Police that its personnel used pellet guns and nail-fitted batons against protesting students during their march to Parliament on July 20. As the committee met, Maken raised the issue and was supported by a number of other opposition MPs, including Priyanka and Senta UBT’s Sanjay Raut. They said the Delhi Police chief should be asked to appear before the committee, insisting that the issue fell within the ambit of crimes against children.Agrawal said the matter is sub judice. With opposition MPs pressing their demand, BJP MP Tarun Chugh said that if members are allowed to raise issues not on the agenda, then he would like the committee to take up the alleged glorification of a Sikh-riots convict, a reference to former Congress MP Sajjan Kumar who died last week while serving his sentence.Chugh’s remarks drew a sharp reaction from Congress MP Jai Prakash, who said the issue was not relevant at all. BJP has accused Congress MP Deepender Hooda of being laudatory in his tribute to Kumar. Hooda has rejected the charge. Agrawal managed to restore order while ruling out a discussion on issues not on the agenda, even as he added that the committee would take up at a later date the issue of SOPs for the use of force against protesters.
Article Summary: Sources said congress mp ajay maken had written to parliamentary committee on home affairs chairperson. Bjp mp tarun chugh said that if members are allowed to raise issues not on the agenda, then he would like the committee to take up the alleged glorification of a sikh-riots convict.

Article Title: Ram Temple donation ‘scam’ whistleblower gets protection from arrest
Article Text:
SC on Tuesday granted interim protection from arrest to Abhishek Upadhyay.

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Tuesday granted interim protection from arrest to Abhishek Upadhyay who claimed he was vindictively booked under SC/ST Act by Ghaziabad police for an alleged road rage incident just because he had exposed embezzlement of donations offered by devotees at the Ram temple in Ayodhya.Appearing for the petitioner, senior advocate Pradeep Rai told a bench of CJI Surya Kant that Upadhyay was the whistleblower and the first to report the alleged misappropriation of monies donated by devotees at the Ayodhya temple.He said since UP Police is vindictive, investigations into the alleged road accident case lodged against him coupled with charges under SC/ST Act should be transferred to an independent agency such as CBI or Delhi Police.Rai complained that police are yet to furnish a copy of the FIR and CCTV camera footage of the alleged accident involving his vehicle and a two-wheeler to the petitioner who is accused of hurling caste-based abuses at the two-wheeler rider after the accident.The bench issued notice to Ghaziabad police and said that “no coercive action shall be taken against the petitioner in the FIR registered at Indirapuram police station, or any such subsequent FIR that may be registered against him in relation to the allegations.”Asking police to furnish a copy of the FIR to the petitioner to enable him to take remedial steps in accordance with the law, the bench said, “As soon as a copy of the FIR is received by the petitioner, he shall be at liberty to approach the jurisdictional high court for seeking relevant relief.”
Article Summary: Sc on tuesday granted interim protection from arrest to abhishek upadhyay. He claimed he was vindictively booked under sc/st act by ghaziabad police for an alleged road rage incident just because he had exposed embezzlement of donations offered by devotees.

Article Title: All Banke Bihari donations must go to deity: Supreme Court
Article Text:
SC said all donations must be deposited in temple donation boxes or credited online into the temple account.

NEW DELHI: The SC Tuesday took strong exception to the report of the court-appointed high-powered committee (HPC) headed by a retired HC judge that donations at Banke Bihari temple at Vrindavan are being pocketed by sevayats and ordered that devotees’ contributions must go only to the temple.Senior advocate Maninder Singh said the sevayats cover the donation box put up by the temple management committee with flowers to prevent devotees from putting their donations into it. These donations are then taken away by the sevayats, he said.Brushing aside the counsel’s submissions that a court decree allows sevayats to keep a part of the donations, a CJI-led bench said all donations must be deposited in temple donation boxes or credited online into the temple account. “First, the donation must be into the dedication, i.e., to the deity. From that you will get your share as part of ‘bhandari’ duties.”
Article Summary: Sc said all donations must be deposited in temple donation boxes or credited online into the temple account. “first, the donation must be into the dedication, i.e. to the deity. From that you will get your share as part of ‘bhandari’ duties,” cji-led bench said.

Article Title: 2013 rape case: Supreme Court directs Tarun Tejpal to surrender within two weeks
Article Text:
Supreme Court denies relief to Tarun Tejpal

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday directed former Tehelka editor Tarun Tejpal to surrender within two weeks in connection with the 2013 Goa sexual assault case.The direction comes after Tejpal challenged the Bombay high court's August 6 judgment, which overturned his acquittal by a trial court and convicted him in the case. The high court sentenced him to 10 years of rigorous imprisonment.The Supreme Court's latest direction means Tejpal will have to surrender before serving the sentence, subject to any further orders in his appeal.The case relates to allegations that Tejpal sexually assaulted a junior colleague inside a hotel elevator in Goa in November 2013 during an event organised by Tehelka magazine.A Goa sessions court had acquitted Tejpal of all charges in May 2021, holding that the prosecution had failed to establish its case beyond reasonable doubt.The Goa government challenged the acquittal before the Bombay High Court, which overturned the trial court's verdict on August 6 and convicted Tejpal.The high court subsequently sentenced him to 10 years of rigorous imprisonment.Tejpal, through advocate Aditya Samaddar, moved the Supreme Court against the Bombay High Court judgment. The Goa government has also approached the Supreme Court seeking a life sentence, arguing that the 10-year punishment was inadequate considering the nature and seriousness of the offences.The case dates back to November 2013, when a junior journalist accused Tejpal of sexually assaulting her inside an elevator at a five-star hotel in Goa.Tejpal was arrested on November 30, 2013, and was later charged under various provisions of the Indian Penal Code, including rape, sexual harassment and assault with intent to disrobe.He had pleaded not guilty to the charges.Following his conviction by the Bombay High Court, Tejpal had told the court that he was 62 years old and the father of two children. He had also claimed that he was being targeted for political reasons.
Article Summary: Supreme court denies relief to tarun tejpal in goa sexual assault case. Former tehelka editor will have to surrender before serving sentence, subject to further orders in his appeal. The high court sentenced him to 10 years of rigorous imprisonment. The goa government has approached the supreme court seeking a life sentence.

Article Title: ‘Do you swim with full suit & coat?’ Rijiju hits back at Khera for mocking swimming video

NEW DELHI: Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju on Tuesday slammed Congress leader Pawan Khera for making "indecent comments" about him after he shared a video of himself swimming in Arunachal Pradesh.In a social media post on X, Rijiju reminded Khera that he has fought eight elections so far, while the Congress leader is a first-term MP, nominated to Rajya Sabha by his party."You are a 1st term MP, nominated by your party in Rajya Sabha & I've fought 8 elections so far. That doesn't give you the right to make indecent comments. I swim with my villagers to inspire my people & followers," Rijiju said."Rahul ji doesn't exist in my mind when I'm with my people. But Congressis started commenting that I can't swim like Rahul Ji. So, I responded since I don't take training for activities. I'm a natural khiladi in our mighty rivers. Don't be abusive needlessly all the time," he added.Rijiju also took a dig at Khera over his spat with Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, saying that he will report the Congress leader's "indiscipline conduct" to Sarma."Dear Pawan Khera, I'll report to CM Himanta Biswa Sarma ji about your indiscipline conduct if you talk about half-naked swimming.Do you swim with full suit & coat?" Rijiju said.Rijiju's reaction came after Khera said that leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has "gotten under BJP's skin", claiming that Rijiju "can’t even go for a half-naked swim without invoking Rahul Gandhi.""Imagine how badly Rahul Ji has gotten under the BJP’s skin. On one hand, Kiren Rijiju can’t even go for a half-naked swim without invoking Rahul Gandhi. On the other, senior citizen Giriraj Singhbjp has been reduced to calling himself a 74-year-old “new baby born”.""What have you done to all of them, Rahul ji?" he added.Earlier, Rijiju shared a video of himself swimming in the rivers of Arunachal Pradesh."Never go to deep water, if you do not know swimming. Many people have drowned in the river. The rivers in Arunachal Pradesh are huge and very deep," he said.Rijiju also shared another video explaining why swimming in the rivers of Arunachal Pradesh is different from swimming in a pool or calmer waters."Some people might think swimming in gushing rivers of Arunachal Pradesh is like swimming in pools or rivers like Yamuna. In raging rivers, our head should be up, not down & body should be more upright, not straight as we keep in swimming competition. Mein yahan ka khiladi hun," he said.
Article Summary: Kiren rijiju shared a video of himself swimming in arunachal pradesh. Congress leader pawan khera made "indecent comments" about him on social media. Union parliamentary affairs minister said he has fought eight elections so far. He also took a dig at khera over his spat with assam chief minister.

Article Title: BPSC exam row, 'dogs bark' remark: What has triggered fresh student protests in Bihar
Article Text:
BPSC protest intensifies as students breach barricades, govt says issues resolved

Govt says students' issues have been addressed

'Do you need 1,800 years?' Students question recruitment delays

Students break through barricades during Raj Bhavan march

JD(U) says govt is serious about students' concerns

Tejashwi writes to Samrat Choudhary

Bihar launches monthly student support camps

NEW DELHI: Chaotic scenes unfolded in Bihar’s Patna on Tuesday as protesting students clashed with police during a massive protest over alleged irregularities in the 70th BPSC examination.The protest was met with a heavy police deployment, with barricades erected to stop the students from marching.Police also used water cannons as protesters attempted to push past the barricades.Later, the Samrat Choudhary-led government claimed it had addressed “almost all issues” raised by the students. The protesters, however, said several long-standing demands remained unresolved and continued their agitation.The students marched from Gandhi Maidan towards Raj Bhavan.The protesting students also broke the barricades in bid to gherao chief minister's residence.The protest has also brought into focus delays in recruitment examinations, the proposed format of the Teacher Recruitment Examination-4 (TRE-4), alleged paper leaks and demands for greater transparency in Bihar's recruitment system.Bihar education minister Mithilesh Tiwari said the government had resolved the issues raised by the students and maintained that its doors remained open for further dialogue."All the issues over which the students were staging a sit-in have been resolved. It is not as if the student agitation was the sole reason for this; it is the government's very intent to resolve the problems faced by our youth in a timely manner. We have addressed every issue raised by the youth. I was surprised to hear a person who has never even taken a board exam offering suggestions on examinations. That is why I would say to Tejashwi Yadav to enroll in a Bihar government school, pass the tenth-grade exam, and then come back to offer us suggestions on examinations," Tiwari said.The minister said that almost all the demands had been met and invited students to approach the government with any remaining concerns."We have met almost all the students' demands. For any students who wish to convey further points to the government, the doors for dialogue remain wide open. Let the students come, talk, and get their issues resolved; the government belongs to them," he said.However, the protesters said their concerns had not been fully addressed and that problems related to the education system, examination paper leaks and delayed recruitment continued.Protester Vikas Bhatt said the students were demanding improvements in Bihar's education system and action against repeated examination paper leaks."Our demand is that the education system in Bihar be improved. We are raising issues regarding the frequent exam paper leaks in the state. Look at the recruitment for librarians, it hasn't happened for 18 years; do you need 1,800 years? Whenever we stage a protest, they simply offer assurances and leave it at that. How can things go on like this? Three recruitment drives were announced through the BSSC, but it has been three years. We have repeatedly besieged the BSSC commission, demanding that the exam dates be announced. Despite this, they keep asking for 15 days' time. Apart from the BPSC, there isn't a single commission in Bihar that issues an annual calendar," Bhatt said.The students are demanding the cancellation of the 70th BPSC examination over allegations of irregularities and paper leaks.The agitation has also centred on the proposed TRE-4 examination. Students have opposed the proposal to conduct the examination in two phases across Bihar and are demanding that it be held in a single phase.They have also sought the immediate release of the official TRE-4 advertisement.As the protest continued, students marched from Gandhi Maidan towards Raj Bhavan. Some protesters broke through police barricades and attempted to move towards the restricted area.Police used water cannons to disperse the crowd, while several protesters were detained.DSP Kamakhya Narayan Singh said the police would not allow the protesters to enter the restricted area, although he expressed hope that the ongoing talks between students and senior officials would lead to a resolution."We will stop them; we won't let them proceed further. However, the dialogue has been positive, and we hope the students will agree. They have raised several issues with the senior officials, and the outcome has been positive. So, I expect the turnout to be lower and that they will agree. If they don't, we will stop them right here. We won't allow them to enter the restricted area," Singh said.Congress leader Sushil Kumar, who was present at the protest site, said the government had failed to give assurances on several key demands."We want to state clearly that a single-stage examination must be implemented for TRE 4.0 at all costs, and negative marking should be abolished. There are numerous other issues as well, regarding the BPSC, BSSC, Sub-Inspector recruitment. The government has offered no assurances on any of these points. We have urged the Chief Minister to hold a dialogue; he should invite our delegation for talks. We have been on a hunger strike for nine days, yet no one is willing to listen to us. Just imagine, had the government engaged in dialogue, this situation would not have arisen. We are heading towards the Chief Minister's residence; the Chief Minister should hold talks, and our delegation will go there for the discussion," Kumar told news agency ANI.JD(U) leader Shravan Kumar said the Bihar government was taking the concerns of students and job seekers seriously and was acting according to established rules and legal provisions."The government is taking the demands and concerns of students and job seekers seriously. Everything is being done for them in accordance with established rules, laws, and provisions. Bihar is the first state in the country to have made such large-scale recruitments across government departments," Kumar said.He also pointed to the government's employment target for the 2025-2030 period and urged young people not to be influenced by the opposition."It is Nitish Kumar's resolve to provide 10 million (1 crore) jobs and employment opportunities to the people of Bihar between 2025 and 2030. Recruitments are taking place in every sector, and vacancies are being announced in every department. I urge our youth to exercise patience and not fall for the opposition's ploys; they are not going to provide jobs. They merely intend to exploit your hard work and sweat to further their own political interests. Beware of them," he added.Meanwhile, Bihar leader of opposition Tejashwi Yadav has written to chief minister Samrat Choudhary over the ongoing BPSC row, urging the government not to ignore the students' demands and to hold talks for an early resolution.Tejashwi has demanded that TRE-4 be conducted as a single examination across the state. He has also sought an end to what he described as discrimination against Hindi-speaking candidates in the BPSC Civil Services Main Examination and interview.The RJD leader has further demanded complete transparency in all competitive examinations, including those for Sub-Inspector, Constable, BSSC and BPSC recruitments.Among his other demands are a high-level independent inquiry into alleged irregularities in past examinations, strict action against recruitment mafias and time-bound schedules for all pending tests.He has specifically called for clear timelines for the BSSC Intermediate, CGL, ASO, BSO, Librarian and Accountant recruitment examinations.RJD scion Tejashwi remark also followed BPSC official's "dog-barking" remark. Bihar LoP also called for action for his remark referring to students.Amid the continuing protests, the Bihar government on Tuesday launched the monthly 'Vidyarthi Sahyog Shivir' or student support camps to address students' grievances.The camps will be organised at educational institutions on the fourth Tuesday of every month, chief minister Samrat Choudhary said in a social media post."The Bihar government is launching Vidyarthi Sahyog Shivir starting today to ensure prompt resolution of students' grievances. These camps will be organised at educational institutions on the fourth Tuesday of every month," Choudhary wrote.The camps will allow students to raise their grievances directly with the concerned government officials. Students will also be able to register complaints online and track their status through the portal and Helpline 1100.The government's announcement comes as the student protest continues in Patna's Gardanibagh area, with the two sides offering sharply different views on whether the protesters' demands have been addressed.
Article Summary: Bihar education minister mithilesh tiwari said the government had resolved the issues raised by the students. The protesters said their concerns had not been fully addressed and that problems related to the education system, examination paper leaks and delayed recruitment continued.

Article Title: Abhishek Banerjee in SC for speedy order on rebel MPs
Article Text:
Abhishek Banerjee

Article Title: 'What women wears is her choice': Rahul Gandhi backs Kriti Sanon over Raksha Bandhan ad row
Article Text:
Kangana slams Kriti Sanon

NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday defended actor Kriti Sanon amid criticism of her outfit in a Raksha Bandhan advertisement, saying "what women wears is her choice."In a post on Instagram, Gandhi said, "What a woman wears, what she does and where she goes - is her choice." "Stop trolling women for exercising their freedom," he added.Rahul's remarks came after Kriti responded to criticism of her jewellery advertisement, released ahead of Raksha Bandhan. The campaign features the actor in an Indo-Western outfit comprising a bralette-inspired blouse, cape and draped skirt while tying a rakhi.The advertisement also drew criticism from actor-turned-politician Kangana Ranaut , who questioned Kriti’s choice of outfit in the campaign.Addressing the controversy in an Instagram post, Kriti had earlier questioned the practice of judging a woman's respect for culture based on her clothes."The essence of festivals is not in the clothes you wear, it is in the emotions and meaning you hold for the traditions. Rakshabandhan is a bond of protection. My sister and I tie rakhi to each other. We know we can protect each other no less than a brother would have," she said.Sanon said she and her sister pray for each other's "health, happiness & long life", adding that the same wishes extend to their dogs because "they are family!"She also questioned the scrutiny faced by women over their clothing. "Also, when will we stop telling women what to wear??” Sanon said.“Ethnic fashion has evolved over the years, but still a woman's respect for her culture is measured with just her clothes!! Culture & Traditions are in her heart, not in her neckline!" she added.Earlier on Monday, BJP MP Kangana Ranaut also slammed Kriti questioning the styling of the advertisement in an Instagram Story."It's a wonderful time to be a woman. Article Title: Vande Mataram row: Is Congress taking a calculated gamble or walking into BJP's trap?
Article Text:
Mallikarjun Kharge, Sonia Gandhi and Rahul at Congress headquarters on Independence Day.

Congress fights back

BJP’s Vande Mataram push

Could Congress have avoided this row

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Is the Congress trying to send out a subtle message signalling “soft minority appeasement”? Or has the party played to BJP’s strength by lapping up a controversy that may push it into a corner?The Congress's decision to sing only two stanzas of Vande Mataram at party events signalled a rare hardening of stance on an issue that the party knows could make it vulnerable to attacks over both minority appeasement and nationalism.As expected, the Congress decision, which cited a 1937 resolution, triggered sharp reactions from the BJP, with Union home minister Amit Shah accusing the Congress of repeating "politics of appeasement."Union minister JP Nadda also slammed the Congress, alleging that the party's 1937 resolution was driven by "appeasement politics" and contributed to the circumstances that led to the Partition. In a post on X, Nadda said the Congress' decision in 1937 to divide 'Vande Mataram' into two parts fuelled the two-nation theory and ultimately led to the partition of the country.'This was followed by attacks questioning Congress’s commitment to nationalism and patriotism.Union minister Giriraj Singh accused the Congress leadership of disrespecting the legacy of India's freedom fighters and operating under ideological pressure. "This is not just opposition to Vande Mataram but against our revolutionaries," Singh said, adding, "Now, the Congress has become the Muslim League. This is not Gandhi ji's Congress but Sonia Gandhi and Rahul Gandhi's Congress," the BJP leader said.BJP MP Dinesh Sharma also accused the opposition leadership of harbouring "Muslim League-like thinking." He equated senior Congress leaders with Muhammad Ali Jinnah, the founder of Pakistan who spearheaded the Two-Nation Theory, to criticise the Congress party's approach toward national symbols.Later, the BJP passed a resolution condemning the Congress Working Committee's decision to sing only the first two stanzas of 'Vande Mataram' and announced a nationwide campaign to raise awareness about the history and significance of the National Song.No surprises here. All these attacks were on expected lines. Surely, the Congress would have anticipated these high-pitched narratives questioning its nationalism and accusing it of appeasement.Congress leaders defended the party's stand, saying 'Vande Mataram' was associated with the freedom struggle and held emotional significance for the Congress. They accused the BJP of politicising the issue and diverting attention from the issue of Ram Mandir donation theft."BJP was not a part of the freedom struggle. Vande Mataram was a part of the freedom struggle; it is emotional for us, but political for them (BJP)," Venugopal said, adding, "We have been reciting Vande Mataram since 1937, more than 90 years. What is new for us?"The Congress leaders alleged that political rivals led by the BJP were deliberately stoking nationalist narratives to cover up their failures. What the Congress perhaps did not realise, or chose to ignore, was that the BJP had already set the stage for bringing Vande Mataram to the centrestage of its politics.Why the 1937 reference created more problems than it solvedBankim Chandra Chatterjee wrote ‘Bande Mataram’ in the late 19th century in Sanskritised Bengali. The original version consisted of six stanzas. The song was first inserted into the pages of his novel, Anandamath, set during the late 18th century when famine and rebellion tore through Bengal.In 1950, alongside ‘Jana Gana Mana’ as the national anthem, Vande Mataram received the honour of a national song following a decision of the Constituent Assembly, under the guidance of Rajendra Prasad, considering the historic role it played in India’s freedom struggle.However, only the first two stanzas of the song were adopted as the national song.The Congress Working Committee (CWC), in a resolution of October 29, 1937, decided that only the first two stanzas of Vande Mataram would be sung at national and public gatherings.This had followed advice from Rabindranath Tagore, who was the first to set Vande Mataram to music and publicly sing it at the 1896 Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress. In a letter to Jawaharlal Nehru, he suggested that only the first two stanzas of the song be used for public and national gatherings.Tagore then noted that the later verses — which invoked Hindu deities like Durga within the context of Bankim Chandra Chatterjee's novel Anandamath—could alienate non-Hindu communities.The fact that the Muslim League and M A Jinnah were among the most vociferous critics of the song made the Congress’s 1937 resolution vulnerable to Muslim appeasement attacks ever since.BJP’s Vande Mataram push began in May this year when the Union Cabinet approved a proposal to amend the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act and put the National Song, Vande Mataram, composed by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee, on the same footing as the National Anthem, Jana Gana Mana.It was during the special discussion of Parliament on “150th Year of Vande Mataram” in December last year that defence minister Rajnath Singh had strongly advocated for elevating the status of Vande Mataram to match the National Anthem. Rajnath had then accused the Congress of historically communalising the song and sidelining it due to appeasement politics.Earlier in January this year the Union home ministry had outlined appropriate conduct and protocols concerning Vande Mataram. The ministry had issued an order that all six stanzas of the official version must be rendered first whenever the National Song and the National Anthem are performed together. It said that the full six-stanza version was to be sung or played on key state occasions.These proposals became law in the just-concluded Monsoon session after Parliament amended the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971, giving Vande Mataram equal legal standing to the National Anthem. The government is also midway through a year-long commemoration of Vande Mataram's 150th anniversary.The amended Act mandates Vande Mataram shall be honoured equally with ‘Jana-Gana-Mana’ and shall have equal status with it, and whoever intentionally prevents the singing of the Indian National Anthem or causes disturbance to any assembly engaged in such singing shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with a fine, or both.Clearly, given the BJP moves, the Congress would have been aware of the political fallout of its Vande Mataram decision. Minority appeasement has been one of the biggest weapons, which the BJP has used very effectively to attack and corner the Congress.In the last 12 years, we have seen the Congress suffer politically over allegations of minority appeasement. The Congress leadership has tried to fight back with a calculated push for soft Hindutva. Rahul Gandhi and other top Congress leaders have visited temples to counter BJP’s attacks on minority appeasement.In the 1980s, the Congress faced a Shah Bano moment, which is still used to target and corner the party over allegations of minority appeasement. The then Congress government led by Rajiv Gandhi enacted a law in Parliament to limit a Muslim husband's maintenance obligation to the three-month iddat period, neutralizing a Supreme Court maintenance order under Section 125 of the Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC).Minorities, especially Muslims, for a very long time were part of Congress’s core vote bank and supported the party electorally. However, as the Congress lost political heft, the minorities gradually shifted to other regional parties. The same happened with other social groups like the SCs, STs and the OBCs. For the last many years, the Congress has been forced to align with the regional parties that weaned away its core voters. Now, as it tries to script its revival, it is trying to win back these communities into the party fold.We have seen Rahul Gandhi aggressively woo the SCs, STs and the OBCs by repeatedly taking up issues that impact them. The Congress leader’s sustained pitch for caste census was an open move to reach out to these core voters. But when it comes to wooing back the minority voters, the Congress perhaps wants to play it safe. And it’s not just the Muslim appeasement attack that the Congress wants to avoid, it perhaps also does not want to antagonize its ally in Uttar Pradesh - the Samajwadi Party.Interestingly, Rahul and Akhilesh Yadav appeal to the same social support base and hence the alliance chemistry is always overshadowed by competing interests.It is in this context that one is left wondering: Has the Congress taken a calculated gamble?
Article Summary: Congress's decision to sing only two stanzas of vande mataram at party events signalled a rare hardening of stance on an issue that the party knows could make it vulnerable to attacks. The congress decision, which cited a 1937 resolution, triggered sharp reactions from the bjp.

Article Title: ICAR registers 16 new breeds of indigenous animals including four cattle
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Expanding the list of well-documented and scientifically recognised animal breeds in the country, the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) has registered 16 more new breeds of indigenous animals including cattle and buffalo, taking the total number of such breeds in India to 262. The move will help in conservation and sustainable utilisation of India’s diverse and climate-resilient animal genetic resources at a time when rising temperature due to global warming is posing grave risk to animal productivity and the overall food security.The new indigenous breeds include four each of cattle (Umarda, Periyar, Koppal and Mahakaushali) and Sheep (Madgyal, Seemanchali, Kow Debar and Asomi); two goats (Totapuri and Battisi); and one each of buffalo (Gomanchali), dog (Kombai), pig (Nagal), horse/pony (Kashmiri), donkey (Braj) and yak (Sikkimese yak).These breeds, registered early this month, represent diverse agro-ecological regions spreading across 13 states -- Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Kerala, Maharashtra, Goa, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Assam, Uttarakhand, Bihar, Nagaland, Sikkim and Tamil Nadu -- and UT of Jammu & Kashmir. Goat breed Battisi is distributed across Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh whereas the sheep breed Madgyal is found in Maharashtra and Karnataka."Indigenous breeds have evolved under diverse production environments and possess locally adapted characteristics that can be valuable for climate resilience, disease adaptation, low-input production, livelihood support and sustainable livestock farming. Their conservation is therefore important not only for maintaining genetic diversity but also for ensuring the availability of adaptive livestock resources for future generations," N H Mohan, directorof the ICAR's National Bureau of Animal Genetic Resources (NBAGR), toldKarnal-based ICAR-NBAGR is the nodal institute for registration of livestock and poultry breeds in India. With the new addition, the indigenous animal breeds now include 59 for cattle (Sahiwal, Gir, Red Kandhari and Hallikar etc.) 23 for buffalo (Murrah, Nili Ravi, Bhadawari and Mehsana etc.), 45 for goat, 50 for sheep, 16 for pigs, nine each for horses & ponies, camel and duck; five for donkey; six for dog and three for yak among others."The new registrations strengthen the national effort to reduce the proportion of nondescript livestock populations through systematic breed identification and documentation. This approach is particularly important for ensuring that valuable locally adapted populations are scientifically recognized and brought within appropriate conservation and sustainable utilization programmes," said Mohan.He said, "ICAR-NBAGR's efforts are aligned with the broader national objective of strengthening India's livestock genetic base and supporting food and nutritional security, sustainable livelihoods and climate-resilient livestock production."
Article Summary: Icar has registered 16 more new breeds of indigenous animals including cattle and buffalo. The move will help in conservation and sustainable utilisation of india’s diverse and climate-resilient animal genetic resources. Rising temperature due to global warming is posing grave risk to animal productivity and the overall food security.

Article Title: Flood-rescued elephant Joymoti airlifted and shifted to Anant Amabani’s Vantara for specialised care
Article Text:
Ensuring the highest standards of welfare during air transport

Joymoti’s story highlights the need for specialised veterinary care facilities closer to where wildlife emergencies occur

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Joymoti, a 53-year-old female elephant rescued from the devastating floods in Nagaland and Assam in July, was airlifted and moved to Vantara, Jamnagar, where she has already begun receiving immediate and specialised veterinary treatment.The elephant was swept away by floodwaters in Nagaland during the second week of July and was subsequently rescued by local communities with the assistance of government agencies. She sustained multiple injuries during the incident, including wounds to her forehead, right ear, the area above her tail, left inner thigh and abdomen, as well as a deep, maggot-infested wound around her external genital area. Her right eye is severely damaged, leaving her blind in that eye, with persistent tearing. She also has longstanding lameness in her left hind leg, resulting from a fracture sustained during logging, which affects her ability to walk normally and access food and water.Following her rescue, Joymoti received first aid and primary veterinary care locally, including wound dressing, pain medication, multivitamin and mineral supplements and supportive treatment. However, given the severity and multiple locations of her injuries, her advancing age and existing mobility challenges, she requires immediate treatment in a specialised hospital setting.Joymoti's transfer to Vantara is solely for immediate and specialised veterinary treatment. The decision to airlift her has been taken with her welfare and medical needs at the centre, allowing her to reach a specialised elephant hospital while minimising the duration and physical demands of ground transportation. Upon arrival at Vantara, Joymoti will undergo a comprehensive veterinary assessment and receive specialised treatment for her injuries and eye condition, along with nutritional and supportive care as required.Transporting an elephant by air for specialised hospital care is an unusual undertaking in India, requiring extensive veterinary, animal-care and logistical planning. Joymoti's transfer is being planned and carried out with careful attention to her health, comfort and safety at every stage, from her veterinary assessment and preparation before travel to loading, monitoring during the flight and her arrival at the hospital.Air transport can significantly reduce the duration of a long-distance journey for an animal requiring urgent medical attention. For elephants with serious injuries, chronic health conditions or mobility challenges, reducing journey time and avoiding prolonged ground travel can be an important consideration in protecting their welfare.Joymoti’s case also highlights the importance of having specialised elephant veterinary care facilities closer to areas where elephants are affected by floods, human-wildlife conflict and other health emergencies.Vantara has proposed the establishment of three wildlife veterinary care centres in Assam, including a dedicated centre for elephants, to strengthen local capacity for wildlife emergency veterinary care. The proposed centres would include species-specific facilities and veterinary support, enabling animals in need to receive timely and appropriate treatment closer to where emergencies occur. The centres would be operated completely independently by the Assam Forest Department.The aim is to strengthen local capacity so that elephants and other wildlife in Assam can receive high-quality care closer to home, avoiding the need for long-distance transportation whenever specialised treatment is required.Joymoti’s journey to Vantara is not a permanent relocation, but an urgent medical transfer undertaken solely to provide the specialised lifesaving treatment she currently requires. Her case underscores the importance of strengthening local veterinary capacity while ensuring that animals requiring advanced care can access it safely and without delay. At Vantara, the immediate priority is to provide Joymoti with the specialised treatment she needs and the best possible chance of recovery and a healthy, safe and dignified life.

She sustained multiple injuries, including wounds to her forehead, right ear, the area above her tail, left inner thigh and abdomen. Her right eye is severely damaged, leaving her blind in that eye, with persistent tearing.

Article Title: A second chance: The uncertainty & struggle behind India's organ transplant boom
Article Text:
Organ transplant in India. Photo credit: AP

India's organ transplant system works through a three-tier hierarchical network coordinated by NOTTO, ROTTO, and SOTTO

The journey begins before surgery

Live Kidneys lead India’s transplant numbers.

“The process is not smooth”

The transplant journey begins long before the operating room, with a long road of tests, paperwork and waiting.

Consent can change the course

Once an organ is allocated, the recipient is prepared for surgery and then closely monitored for complications and organ function

Living donation : another route, but not a simple one

Following the surgery, transplant centres also continue monitoring recipient information and clinical status.

The surgery is only the beginning

The emotional toll of transplantation

Recovery brings a new set of challenges

Behind every transplant statistic is a patient who has waited, a donor who has made an extraordinary decision, and a family navigating a system in which every clearance, consent and organ offer can change the course of a life.

Beyond the numbers

India’s transplant system has grown rapidly, from 4,990 transplants in 2013 to 20,138 in 2025. But for a patient, a transplant is far more than a surgical procedure. It is a journey through medical tests, clearances, documentation, waiting, uncertainty, organ matching and, eventually, surgery and lifelong follow-up.Transplant hospitals and coordinators are at the centre of this system, working within the wider network of the National Organ and Tissue Transplant Organisation (NOTTO), Regional Organ and Tissue Transplant Organisations (ROTTOs) and State Organ and Tissue Transplant Organisations (SOTTOs).Yet statistics and institutional structures can obscure what the process actually feels like for the person waiting for an organ. For recipients such as Hemant Kumar Thakur and Shrishti Sinha, the reality is one of uncertainty, exhaustion and fear — followed by the possibility of a second chance at life.A patient with advanced organ failure is first evaluated at a registered transplant centre. The assessment can involve blood tests, imaging, organ-specific investigations and evaluation by a multidisciplinary team. If found medically suitable, the patient is registered in the relevant transplant system.Being on a waiting list, however, does not simply mean waiting in chronological order. Allocation depends on the organ and applicable rules, including factors such as medical urgency, compatibility and, for some organs, time spent on the list. NOTTO’s framework also provides for urgent and super-urgent categories. For kidney patients, for instance, time on dialysis is among the factors considered.NOTTO coordinates the system nationally, while ROTTOs and SOTTOs connect regional and state-level transplant activity. The State Appropriate Authority separately oversees regulatory compliance, including the registration of transplant centres and adherence to legal and ethical requirements.For recipients, however, the elaborate network can feel much simpler: a long wait, a stream of tests and paperwork, and the constant question of what happens next.Hemant Kumar Thakur, from Jamshedpur, Jharkhand, underwent a kidney transplant at Apollo Hospitals in Kolkata, with his wife, Kanchan Mala, donating a kidney. For him, the hardest part was not the operation but navigating the process beforehand.Because he lived in Jharkhand while the transplant took place in West Bengal, Hemant had to deal with inter-state approvals and paperwork.“Because the procedure involved two different states — Jharkhand and West Bengal — I had to obtain No Objection Certificates (NOCs) from both states before the transplant could proceed,” he said.Despite the difficulties, Hemant was fortunate to have a compatible donor within his family.“The process is not smooth; it is quite challenging. I was lucky that the match was found within my own family, with my wife,” he said.His experience also made him aware of the uncertainty faced by patients without a matching family donor. He recalled seeing patients who had found donors and completed much of the paperwork, only for the donor to later withdraw.“After going through the entire process, they were back where they had started — back to square one,” he said.India’s transplant framework is governed by the Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues Act, 1994 (THOTA) and related rules. Organ donation must be voluntary and free from commercial dealings, while transplantation is permitted only through authorised institutions.Dr Ankur Garg, GI Surgeon and Liver Transplant Specialist at Paras Health in Gurugram, says legitimate organisations and transplant coordinators play an important role in educating patients, facilitating listing and supporting families when brain-stem death is declared.But he warns that patients can also be targeted by unscrupulous intermediaries.“There will always be unsocial elements, touts, agents in society luring needy patients and families and giving false hopes and promises of early organ allocation, lesser waiting times and so much extra,” he said.Consent can also change during the donation process. Dr Garg explains that once brain-stem death has been declared and the family consents to donation, the process of identifying eligible recipients begins. But consent can still be withdrawn before organ retrieval.“Before wheeling into the operation theatre where organ harvesting happens, anyone can withdraw consent, and the whole process will stop,” he said.For recipients, that possibility can mean losing an organ they had been preparing to receive and returning to the uncertainty of the waiting list.Not every patient has to depend on a deceased donor. Certain organs, particularly kidneys and part of the liver, can be donated by living donors after medical, legal and ethical evaluation.The donor’s compatibility and health are assessed, while the legal process depends partly on the relationship between donor and recipient. Near-relative donations follow the applicable framework, while other living-donor relationships may require scrutiny by an Authorisation Committee.Dr Garg says a patient cannot simply register at multiple centres and wait for whichever offers an organ first.“As per the rule, any patient is allowed to register at one place only. Under NOTTO guidelines and Indian transplant regulations, a patient cannot be registered on a deceased donor waiting list at multiple hospitals or centres simultaneously,” he said.He said the listing process requires a medical summary, blood group, relevant reports and valid Aadhaar or national identification.Once an organ is allocated, the recipient is prepared for surgery and then closely monitored for complications and organ function. But leaving the hospital does not mean leaving the transplant journey behind.Recipients must take prescribed immunosuppressive medicines consistently, attend follow-up appointments and undergo regular investigations. Transplant centres also continue monitoring recipient information and clinical status.Hemant said his own transplant was comparatively smooth once the approvals and paperwork were completed, but the financial and medical commitments continued.He spent approximately Rs 15–20 lakh on the transplant and related treatment in 2020.“I do not have any additional complications. I just go for routine check-ups every six months and have to take medication for the rest of my life,” he said.He currently spends around Rs 7,000–8,000 a month on medicines, although he noted that aftercare and medication costs vary between patients.Hemant also contrasted the long-term experience of the recipient with that of his living donor, his wife.“The donor has to take medicines for about three months after the transplant and can lead a normal life,” he said.Shrishti Sinha, an engineer who now works as a freelancer in Delhi, describes her transplant journey through a different lens: uncertainty, gratitude, fear and the possibility of rebuilding a future.“There are many moments of uncertainty. There are medical tests, clearances, waiting for updates and constantly wondering what comes next,” she says.Even hope was fragile.“Not completely. As if one moment hope was rising, the next it was gone. There were cases more severe than mine, or someone who had a higher percentage of surviving,” she recalls.Shrishti underwent treatment at R&R Hospital in Delhi and remembers her doctors as a source of encouragement.“It was R&R Hospital, Delhi, and the doctors were positive and kept trying to cheer me up,” she says.When she finally realised she would receive an organ, her response was deeply personal.“I was crying and feeling grateful that I was going to live, that I would get to spend more time with my husband and create a future,” she recalls.The transplant did not instantly restore normal life. Shrishti found recovery difficult, from eating and drinking to physiotherapy.“Recovery was not straightforward. There were challenges with eating, drinking and physiotherapy. Seeing the scar for the first time was scary,” she says.There were unexpected experiences, too.“The weirdest thing was having strange cravings that I never used to have,” she recalls.Five years later, however, she says the biggest change is her ability to think beyond her illness.“The biggest change is that I can think about the future again. Before the transplant, so much of my life revolved around my health and whether my condition would deteriorate further.”She now marks the day of her operation as something more than a medical milestone.“Five years later, I have started treating my operation day as my second birthday, a chance to live,” she says.India’s transplant system may be measured in hospitals, registries, waiting lists and annual numbers. But for the person inside it, transplantation is much more intimate: months of paperwork, uncertainty and waiting, followed by surgery and the lifelong responsibility of protecting the new organ.Behind every transplant statistic is a patient who has waited, a donor who has made an extraordinary decision, and a family navigating a system in which every clearance, consent and organ offer can change the course of a life.For recipients like Hemant and Shrishti, the transplant is ultimately not just about surviving. It is about being able to imagine tomorrow again.
Article Summary: India’s transplant system has grown rapidly, from 4,990 transplants in 2013 to 20,138 in 2025. But for a patient, a transplant is far more than a surgical procedure. It is a journey through medical tests, clearances, documentation, waiting, uncertainty, organ matching and, eventually, surgery.

Article Title: 'Shameful': UP Congress to boycott TV debates with Ayodhya priest after spokesperson abused
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh Congress unit on Tuesday announced that none of its spokespersons will participate in TV debates with Ayodhya's Hanuman Garhi Temple priest Raju Das, accusing him of abusing and threatening party spokesperson Kunwar Singh Nishad during a live debate.UP Congress media department chairman and former minister CP Rai said Das crossed "all limits of decency" during a debate on Doordarshan News on Monday.In a statement, the party alleged that Das used obscene and abusive language against Nishad, including abusing his mother and issuing threats."The two women anchors of DD News who were part of the debate were also stunned, and the debate had to be stopped midway," Rai said, describing the incident as "shameful and unforgivable".The Congress also demanded an impartial examination of the original recording, video footage and digital evidence of the programme. It said strict action should be taken according to law if the allegations are found to be true.The Congress said political differences should be addressed through arguments and not personal abuse or threats."Congress workers are not afraid of abuse. We believe in the Constitution and the law, and believe in answering every question democratically," Rai said.The controversy comes amid a political row over a purported fish feast at a Nishad community event in Ayodhya, attended by UP Congress chief Ajay Rai during the Hindu holy month of Sawan.The Bharatiya Janata Party and chief minister Yogi Adityanath had attacked Rai over the alleged feast, while the Congress has maintained that there was no proof that its state president had eaten fish.Rai had challenged Adityanath to produce a photograph or video showing him eating fish or being present at the place where it was cooked. He said he would apologise and resign as state Congress president if such evidence was produced.The Congress has defended the food traditions of the Nishad community, while BJP leaders have criticised the alleged consumption of fish during Sawan in Ayodhya.
Article Summary: Ayodhya's hanuman garhi temple priest raju das accused of abusing and threatening party spokesperson kunwar singh nishad. Up congress media department chairman and former minister cp rai said das crossed "all limits of decency" during a debate on doordarshan news on monday.

Article Title: Surrender within 3 weeks, SC tells ex-Tehelka editor Tarun Tejpal
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Tuesday directed former Tehelka editor Tarun Tejpal to first surrender within three weeks, saying that his appeal against conviction and 10-year imprisonment in a rape case would be heard only thereafter.Justice Alok Aradhe rejected Tejpal’s plea for exemption from surrendering and asked him to file a surrender certificate before it. Senior advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for Tejpal, sought three weeks’ time to surrender, the bench granted him time to surrender.Goa govt opposed his plea for exemption from surrendering and said his appeal was not admissible since he had not filed a separate application seeking exemption from surrender or shown a certificate that he has already surrendered as per Order XXII Rule 5 of the Supreme Court Rules, 2013.The Goa bench of Bombay HC convicted Tejpal under multiple provisions of Indian Penal Code (IPC) and sentenced him to 10 years’ rigorous imprisonment each under Sections 376(2)(f) and 376(2)(k), with the sentences to run concurrently.The case relates to two alleged incidents at Grand Hyatt in Goa during Tehelka’s THiNK Fest in Nov 2013. The high court found the victim’s evidence consistent and credible despite extensive cross-examination. The case against Tejpal involves allegations that he sexually assaulted a junior colleague twice in 2013, in an elevator of a high-end hotel in Goa.The Goa Police subsequently registered an FIR against Tarun Tejpal.

Article Title: NMC pushes old doctors to re-register, but can’t net new ones
Article Text:
Based on MBBS seats and pass rates, at least 68,000 new doctors should have registered to practice.

NMC pushes old docs to re-register, but can’t net new ones

National Medical Commission (NMC) is seeking to re-register around 11 lakh doctors to create an updated national medical registry, yet it has failed to register even fresh entrants to the profession despite many state registries sharing records every year, reports Rema Nagarajan.Based on MBBS seats and pass rates, at least 68,000 new doctors should have registered to practice, but only 44,400 entries were recorded in 2025 with at least 24,000 graduates missing in Indian Medical Register. The gap points to potential failure of NMC to sync state and national registries, as required under NMC Act.The National Medical Commission (NMC) is pushing a regulation to make about 11 lakh doctors re-register to create an updated national medical registry, but it has failed to even register fresh entrants to the profession despite many state registries sending it new entries every year.With over 91,000 MBBS seats available in 2020-21, even with an estimated 75-90% pass percentage, at least 68,000 MBBS graduates should have registered to practice in 2025. Yet the Indian Medical Register shows just over 44,400 entries. That means at least 24,000 of those who graduated just last year are missing from the registry.If thousands of foreign medical graduates who register each year are included, the number of freshly minted doctors missing from the registry would be even more.For instance, in 2023, over 10,000 foreign medical graduates passed the qualifying exam, after which they have to complete a mandatory one-year internship before receiving permanent registration that would make them eligible to practice in India. So, most of these 10,000 would have registered in 2025. Thus, the total number of doctors registering in 2025 would be roughly 80,000, but just over half the number (55%) have been added to the registry.Most of the doctors would have registered with state medical councils. However, new entries in state medical council registries are not being reflected in the national registry as the NMC is yet to synchronise all state registries with the national registry. The NMC Act, 2019, had mandated such synchronisation. It is yet to happen, almost six years after the NMC was constituted in Sept 2020. Neither is NMC adding the new entries that many state councils send every year.Take Assam Medical Council, for instance. It is a state with only govt medical colleges. In the national registry, there are a total of 25,722 registrations from the state council. It shows only one entry for 2025, zero for 2024 and 2023, 106 entries for 2022 and 353 in 2021. The website shows 890 registered in 2024. There were over 720 seats in Assam in 2015 and 1,000 seats in 2020. How is NMC accepting zero entries in 2023 and 2024, or only 106 in 2022?Similarly, NMC’s registry has a total of 67,142 entries from Kerala with just seven entries in 2025 and 17 in 2024. In 2014, Kerala had 3,650 MBBS seats, which increased to 4,500 by 2020. “We are sending details every year... In the name of a new updated NMR, they are not updating the existing one,” said KSMC chief Dr Harikumaran Nair.If the NMC were to register only those who became doctors in the last five years, including foreign medical graduates, it would have had an updated registry of over 3.5 lakh doctors (32%) of the estimated 11 lakh who are said to be available.
Article Summary: Based on mbbs seats and pass rates, at least 68,000 new doctors should have registered to practice. But only 44,400 entries were recorded in 2025 with at least 24,000 graduates missing in indian medical register. The gap points to potential failure of nmc to sync state and national registries, as required under nmc act.
